record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a tool that uses harmful-minus-harmless refusal vectors to steer an abliterated model, but does not report benchmark results or test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The README describes the demo as changing unsafe support-ticket responses from compliance to refusal. It also says steering strength matters, but gives no measured results. The benchmark section lists metrics and how to run the suite, not benchmark outcomes.
record.test_reason: A tool repo. It extracts an Arditi harmful-minus-harmless vector from aligned Qwen3-8B and adds it to an abliterated Qwen3-8B to force refusal on detected threats. The README reports no measured refusal rates, ablation results or benchmark outcomes. The only result statement is a qualitative demo claim, and the steering is deliberately induced as a defence tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README presents a demo that detects jailbreaks and prompt injections via Jacobian-lens readouts and steers an abliterated Qwen3-8B toward in-role refusal. It reports no benchmark outcomes; it describes only the scorecard metrics and how to run the suite.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo, not a replication. It states that it extracts harmful-minus-harmless vectors at the last prompt token from aligned Qwen/Qwen3-8B and applies them to an abliterated Qwen3-8B at selected layers; no experimental comparison with the original method is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says alpha that is too low keeps compliance and alpha that is too high produces gibberish; it gives no specific values for these cases.

fits_no_version.finding: The README asserts that adding an aligned-model refusal vector, plus a refusal system prompt, makes an abliterated Qwen3-8B refuse unsafe support tickets. Alpha too low keeps compliance; alpha too high yields gibberish. No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal direction from an aligned model can restore refusal in its abliterated variant when added at inference, within a working range of steering strength.

record.problems: No benchmark results, sample-level outcomes, uncertainty estimates, or evidence of a run are reported in the README. The described response change is a qualitative demo claim.
record.rows_left_out: No benchmark rows: the README describes a 500-case suite and its metrics, but reports no scorecard values. The file list contains benchmark result placeholders, not results.

untested.parts: No ablation test, no measured induction rate on harmless prompts, no capability check.
Uses an existing abliterated model (huihui-ai) but does not measure its refusal rate or test the weight edit.
No analysis of whether jailbreaks suppress the direction; no adversarial training.
Applies a vector from aligned Qwen3-8B to its abliterated variant, which is implicitly a cross-variant transfer, but reports no measured outcome.
Qwen3-8B has a thinking mode, but no reasoning-model-specific test is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The README was read; the code was not. The benchmark_results directories contain only .gitkeep, so no scorecard exists in the repo. The re-steering of an abliterated model with an aligned-model vector bears on V2 and V6 in spirit, but it is unmeasured.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test of ablation, harmless-request refusal, or preservation of other abilities.
The README uses an already abliterated model; it does not test a weight edit or report its effect.
No test of whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
No test comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account.
No test separating harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No test of how refusal training affects the existence of a removable direction.

rows.subject: huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3-8B-abliterated-v2
rows.operation_detail: Apply an Arditi-style refusal vector extracted from harmful-minus-harmless prompts to the model's residual stream.

conditions.value: aligned Qwen/Qwen3-8B; harmful minus harmless at the last prompt token
steered; REFUSAL_SYSTEM supplies the redirect wording

rows.baseline: Compliance and forbidden tool calls (as described for the undefended path)
rows.value: The README says unsafe tickets flip to an in-role refusal with an allowed alternative.
rows.note: This is a qualitative functionality statement, not a reported benchmark result. It concerns unsafe requests and therefore does not measure V1's harmless-request condition.
rows.check: This is a qualitative functionality description ('unsafe tickets flip... to a short in-role refusal'), not a measured result. No rate, no sample size and no control are given. The refusal wording is also shaped by a REFUSAL_SYSTEM prompt on the steered path, which confounds attributing the refusal to the vector alone. It arguably should not be a result row; it is kept only as a description of use.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
